screens.name: Home — unavailable omen and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 08–09 show a dominant gold orb, explicit asking instructions and an unavailable-omen explanation, with similar composition across captures.
findings: Increase the prominence of the example question above the orb, especially against changing mist.

screens.name: Home — successful omen fixture
screens.evidence: Sheet 08 shows a readable omen beneath the hero while the example question is extremely faint in this capture.
findings: Keep the example question consistently readable throughout the entrance.

screens.name: Approach — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 preserves the orb-led composition, and supplied runtime evidence reports automatic advancement after 650ms with an immediate reduced-motion alternative.
findings: Verify that this brief automatic transition neither strands focus nor creates redundant screen-reader announcements.

screens.name: Ask — normal and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 02 shows a labeled multiline question, visible usage balance and distinct typing and voice actions in consistent paired layouts.
findings: Replace the technical phrase “your prediction engine” with a plain description of where submitted questions go.

screens.name: Ask — enlarged text
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 shows the enlarged question and a fully visible submission button, with the decorative orb omitted.
findings: Verify submission visibility and question editing with a physical mobile keyboard open.

screens.name: Voice unavailable — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 09 prioritizes Type your question and displays a microphone-permission recovery notice beneath a secondary retry action.
findings: Place the voice failure explanation closer to the typing fallback so the reason for the changed task is immediately apparent.

screens.name: Planning — loading and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 11 shows a specific planning description, an approximate wait, a no-charge assurance and Cancel beneath the orb.
findings: Verify that prolonged loading and cancellation are announced clearly through assistive technology.

screens.name: Question 1 — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 02 shows four spacious answer rows and progress, while runtime evidence reports keyboard advancement and focus transfer.
findings: Make immediate advancement predictable before the first answer is selected.

screens.name: Question 2 — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 03 maintains the question, answer-row and progress structure across the second-question captures.
findings: Verify that returning to this question exposes the previous selection visually and through its accessible name.

screens.name: Question 3 — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 03 shows the final numbered question with the same four-row treatment and restrained progress indicator.
findings: Clarify that choosing the final answer starts prediction generation.

screens.name: Question — keyboard-focused heading
screens.evidence: Sheet 01 visibly outlines the new question heading, and runtime evidence reports that Tab reaches the first answer.
findings: Align the heading-focus treatment with the gold settings-focus treatment while preserving strong visibility.

screens.name: Custom answer — empty and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 shows question context, a Your answer label, Change, a multiline field and a visibly muted Continue button.
findings: Make the required-answer condition explicit instead of relying solely on the muted Continue treatment.

screens.name: Custom answer — enlarged empty
screens.evidence: Sheet 04 retains the complete enlarged question, input label, Change control and submission button.
findings: Verify that Change and the field remain separately discoverable at native text enlargement.

screens.name: Custom answer — enlarged filled
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 shows a wrapped entered answer and a fully readable two-line Reveal my prediction button.
findings: Verify longer entered answers without losing the question context or submission access.

screens.name: Custom answer — synthetic keyboard constraint
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 exposes the answer and submission button but not the full question context, while supplied browser evidence reports retained context in the constrained viewport.
findings: Capture and verify the complete editing viewport on a physical phone to resolve the context visibility uncertainty.

screens.name: Research — loading and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 11–12 preserve the loading composition while changing the explanation to current-context research and prediction formation.
findings: Announce the stage change once without repeatedly interrupting assistive-technology users.

screens.name: Planning error — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 06 shows an explicitly failed fixture reading, a no-charge assurance and prominent retry with question editing.
findings: Verify that repeated failure preserves the question and leaves editing reachable.

screens.name: Prediction error — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 06 adds Review answers to the retry and editing recovery choices without presenting failure as a result.
findings: Verify that reviewing answers after failure restores every prior answer, including custom text.

screens.name: Reveal — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 12–13 show a dominant prediction, uncertainty label, expandable rationale, check-back date and prominent sharing action.
findings: Reduce the competition among the four secondary actions below Share by grouping editing and answer review.

screens.name: Reveal — expanded rationale and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 12 shows the rationale opening below the unchanged hero and headline, leaving only the start of a long fixture explanation visible.
findings: Bring the expanded explanation into view and structure long rationale content into readable sections.

screens.name: Check-in — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 04–05 place three outcome choices beneath the saved prediction and above its check-back date and sharing button.
findings: Give the outcome choices a clearer grouped-control treatment so their purpose is distinguishable from navigation links.

screens.name: Saved outcome — Yes
screens.evidence: Sheet 10 shows a checkmarked Yes, inline saved status and confirmation notice, with persistence supported by supplied runtime evidence.
findings: Keep the inline status as the durable confirmation and ensure the additional notice does not conceal remaining actions.

screens.name: Saved outcome — Not quite
screens.evidence: Sheet 09 shows matching Not quite wording in the selected choice and saved status, alongside a history confirmation.
findings: Verify that changing this saved outcome announces the replacement without duplicate live messages.

screens.name: Saved outcome — Not yet
screens.evidence: Sheet 10 explicitly distinguishes the saved pending outcome using Not yet text, a checkmark and a waiting confirmation.
findings: Preserve the pending distinction wherever this result appears in History and reminders.

screens.name: History — empty and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 08 pairs an empty-history explanation with Ask the Ball and identifies storage as local to the device.
findings: Give the empty-state Ask the Ball action stronger visual prominence.

screens.name: History — populated and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 07 distinguishes entry date, original question, prediction and check-back date in a restrained editorial row.
findings: Make the row’s ability to reopen a reading more discoverable.

screens.name: History — stress list and persisted outcome
screens.evidence: Sheet 07 shows repeated rows extending below the tab bar and a saved Came true status, with persistence reported in runtime evidence.
findings: Verify the final row and all its actions can scroll fully above the fixed tab bar at enlarged text sizes.

screens.name: Sky — sample/offline and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 16 discloses offline sample stars, marks Love with a checkmark and keeps Ask this too fully visible.
findings: Verify the scattered star choices have predictable keyboard order and sufficiently large nonoverlapping targets.

screens.name: Circles — offline
screens.evidence: Sheet 05 explains the offline state, offers Retry and shows muted creation and sharing controls that runtime evidence identifies as disabled.
findings: Associate the disabled creation control directly with the offline explanation.

screens.name: Plans — normal and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 10–11 show selected annual pricing, monthly pricing, reading packs and repeated explicit simulation labels.
findings: Verify that complete billing terms and restoration controls remain reachable beneath the visible options.

screens.name: Plans — enlarged text
screens.evidence: Sheet 10 stacks enlarged plan details clearly but captures the primary continuation button partly below the viewport.
findings: Demonstrate a fully visible continuation button and reachable remaining plan options after scrolling at 200% text.

screens.name: Sensitive redirect — plan and prediction fixtures with transitions
screens.evidence: Sheets 13–14 consistently prioritize support, explain the fixture redirect and state that no reading or memory was consumed.
findings: Verify focus lands on the redirect explanation and that the support action has a clear external destination announcement.

screens.name: Sensitive redirect — actual classifier, normal
screens.evidence: Sheet 14 shows an actual classifier response with prominent support, direct care-oriented guidance and alternate question actions.
findings: Verify the external support destination and return path, which the supplied runtime evidence explicitly leaves untested.

screens.name: Sensitive redirect — actual classifier, enlarged
screens.evidence: Sheet 14 keeps the enlarged support button visible but dedicates substantial initial space to the headline before guidance continues below the viewport.
findings: Reduce enlarged headline dominance so more immediately useful guidance appears alongside the support action.

screens.name: Share — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 15 shows a small portrait preview and separate image, video and invitation commands, while supplied evidence verifies PNG but not successful MP4 output.
findings: Explain video availability before activation when encoding support cannot be confirmed.

screens.name: Story preview — settled and transition
screens.evidence: Sheet 16 presents a larger portrait card and a correctly labeled Download image action, with Back to sharing partly below the capture.
findings: Ensure the return action can be fully exposed above the bottom safe area.

screens.name: You — empty memory, settings and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 15 and 17 separate plan information, empty memory and preferences, with runtime evidence supporting preference activation and persistence.
findings: Remove or differentiate the duplicated See plans and View plans and credits entry points.

screens.name: You — populated real memory
screens.evidence: Sheet 17 displays three facts from the actual Ollama flow with Edit and Forget actions, whose recovery paths are reported in runtime evidence.
findings: Verify each repeated Edit and Forget control announces the associated fact.

screens.name: Settings — keyboard focus
screens.evidence: Sheet 15 shows a strong full-row focus outline, and supplied controls evidence reports 342×52px targets and keyboard activation.
findings: Carry this clear focus treatment consistently across other interactive controls.

screens.name: Settings — enlarged text
screens.evidence: Sheet 14 shows enlarged preference labels and tab captions, with lower privacy content partially obscured at the visible scroll position.
findings: Verify the entire privacy action clears the fixed navigation when scrolled into view.

components.name: Hero orb
components.evidence: The gold illustrated orb supplies a consistent focal point across sheets, and supplied evidence reports browser animation performance and reduced-motion stopping.
findings: Verify its accessible role distinguishes the actionable Home orb from decorative instances.

components.name: Tab bar
components.evidence: Sheets 07–09 and 14–17 show labeled icons, an elevated Ask orb and underlined selected destinations, including enlarged labels.
findings: Verify enlarged labels and touch targets remain comfortable on physical devices with bottom safe areas.

components.name: Wordmark and balance header
components.evidence: Home uses a script wordmark and screens consistently place a small remaining-usage balance at the upper right.
findings: Use “1 reading left today” where space permits to make the balance self-explanatory.

components.name: Primary button
components.evidence: Cream filled buttons consistently dominate action areas and wrap their labels successfully in several enlarged captures.
findings: Verify pressed, busy and disabled distinctions across every primary action, beyond the demonstrated browser paths.

components.name: Secondary action
components.evidence: Gold text links and divider rows provide secondary actions, but several screens place multiple similarly weighted actions together.
findings: Standardize target padding and group related secondary actions to reduce scanning effort.

components.name: Answer choice
components.evidence: Sheets 01–03 show spacious borderless answer rows, with supplied runtime evidence supporting Space/Enter advancement and restored answers.
findings: Provide a perceptible selected or pressed acknowledgment before immediate advancement.

components.name: Question input
components.evidence: Sheet 02 shows a persistent label and readable multiline question inside a strong gold outline with an additional lower rule.
findings: Simplify the doubled lower-edge treatment while retaining an unmistakable input boundary.

components.name: Large-text input
components.evidence: Sheets 01, 04 and 05 show wrapped enlarged inputs and visible submission controls, with only synthetic keyboard coverage supplied.
findings: Verify physical keyboard resizing, caret visibility and long-answer scrolling at native text enlargement.

components.name: Settings switch
components.evidence: Sheets 14–15 show distinct thumb positions, full-row focus and enlarged labels, with measured browser targets and persistence reported.
findings: Verify native assistive technology announces each preference name, role and current value.

components.name: Omen content
components.evidence: Sheets 08–09 distinguish a successful fixture omen from an unavailable state with an explicit alternative action.
findings: Give the asking alternative a direct control within the unavailable-omen section.

components.name: Sky stars and selected question
components.evidence: Sheet 16 connects a checkmarked category to its sample question and a fully visible primary action.
findings: Verify each star has a generous target and exposes its selected state independently of color.

components.name: Circle surface
components.evidence: Sheet 05 states what circles share, displays offline recovery and explains an age-related sharing restriction.
findings: Distinguish offline-disabled controls from age-restricted controls with directly associated explanations.

components.name: History row
components.evidence: Sheet 07 separates dates, questions, predictions and outcome metadata without introducing heavy cards.
findings: Expose each row as a clearly named actionable reading with its saved outcome included.

components.name: Plan option
components.evidence: Sheets 10–11 show annual selection using a checkmark and divider, explicit billing cadence and stacked enlarged prices.
findings: Verify the options behave and announce themselves as one mutually exclusive selection group.

components.name: Share preview
components.evidence: Sheets 15–16 show a consistent portrait export design, while its disclaimer and branding become very small in the compact preview.
findings: Provide an accessible text equivalent and an obvious route to inspect the preview at readable size.

components.name: Notice and recovery
components.evidence: Sheets 09–10 show explicit voice failure and saved-outcome notices with Dismiss, and runtime evidence reports inline live outcome status.
findings: Verify notices do not cover required controls or produce duplicate screen-reader announcements.

components.name: Typography
components.evidence: The sheets consistently combine expressive serif headings with plain supporting text, but enlarged headlines consume substantial vertical space.
findings: Tune enlarged heading proportions and paragraph spacing to preserve useful context above the fold.

components.name: Atmospheric background
components.evidence: The dark mist and gold glow remain coherent across the sheets, with supplied browser contrast, frame-performance and reduced-motion checks.
findings: Extend contrast and motion checks to remaining screens and physical-device rendering before certification.

limitations: All grades are provisional: this evaluation uses the attached sheets and supplied runtime account, without independently executing checks or inspecting underlying evidence files.
Every dimension is scored independently; null denotes an inapplicable dimension, not missing evidence.
Aesthetic dimension scores of 9 describe visible strengths only and do not certify a screen or component at 9/10.
The authorized A >=9 and F >=9 threshold is not met; no screen or component receives 9/10 certification.
Paired transition images support compositional continuity, but cannot establish animation timing, focus continuity or freedom from transient layout shifts.

Reported browser checks support keyboard handling, persistence, contrast, reduced motion and sampled performance; physical Safari, native text scaling, keyboard safe areas, VoiceOver/TalkBack, microphone hardware and haptics remain unverified.
Content extending below a screenshot is not proof of an unreachable action; scrolling and safe-area access remain unverified where not specifically supported.
Synthetic predictions and rationale text establish layout coverage only; fixture wording is not treated as a production-copy defect or evidence of predictive quality.
PNG export is reported as demonstrated; successful MP4 encoding, OS share delivery, real billing and configured social services are not demonstrated.
The actual sensitive redirect is represented, but its external support destination was not exercised.
No definite hard-gate failure is established by these screenshots; inaccessible hidden controls or failed native behavior cannot be ruled out.
topFixes: Verify physical-phone keyboard, text enlargement, safe areas and screen-reader flows before seeking 9/10 certification.
Resolve the constrained custom-input context uncertainty and demonstrate fully reachable enlarged Plans and Settings actions.
Bring expanded rationale into view and structure long explanations for scanning.
Explain Story video availability before users attempt an unverified export path.
Standardize focus, secondary-action targets and immediate answer-selection feedback.
Reduce enlarged headline dominance and strengthen faint Home example text.
